target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): route shared OTLP endpoints per signal
target.body:
Related: #98886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators enabling multiple diagnostics OTLP signals could send metrics and logs payloads to a traces endpoint when their shared OTLP endpoint already ended in `/v1/traces`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared diagnostics OTLP endpoint fallback now rewrites only a trailing OTLP signal segment to the requested signal path, while explicit traces, metrics, and logs endpoint overrides remain exact per-signal routes. The OpenTelemetry gateway docs now describe that split so shared endpoints and exact signal overrides stay predictable.

## User Impact

Operators can point `diagnostics.otel.endpoint` or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` at a signal-qualified OTLP HTTP URL and enable traces, metrics, and logs without misrouting non-trace payloads. Existing explicit per-signal endpoint overrides keep their current exact behavior.

## Evidence

- Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts` → 1 file, 97 tests passed (includes the shared-endpoint rewrite and explicit-override exact-route regression tests). Re-run green after the follow-up refactor commit.
- Live OTLP loopback (real-behavior, no mocks): drove the real `@opentelemetry/exporter-*-otlp-proto` v2 exporters (trace/metric/log) against a `127.0.0.1` HTTP receiver with a single shared signal-qualified endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/api/public/otel/v1/traces?timeout=30s#tenant-a` and all three signals enabled, then recorded the paths each payload actually POSTed to:
  - **Before (old resolver):** metrics and logs both hit `…/v1/traces?timeout=30s` — real misrouting.
  - **After (this PR):** traces→`…/v1/traces`, metrics→`…/v1/metrics`, logs→`…/v1/logs`; the `?timeout=30s` query is preserved on the wire and the `#tenant-a` fragment is dropped (client-side per HTTP spec, never transmitted).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` clean.
- Dependency contract: OpenTelemetry Node OTLP/HTTP exporters POST each signal to its own `v1/{traces,metrics,logs}` resource path; a shared endpoint used for multiple signals must be re-pathed per signal, which the loopback above confirms on the wire.
- AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the fix; I reviewed, ran a multi-angle code review, folded in a dedup/comment refactor, and produced the live proof above. I understand the code path.
- Proof gaps: loopback receiver is a stub (records paths, returns empty 200); no live vendor backend (Langfuse/Grafana Cloud) run — the routing being verified is client-side URL shaping, which the real exporters exercise identically against any collector.
